title: The button does nothing
summary: Wire a browser event so the storefront cart responds to a real click.

scenario.briefing: The Add to cart button has a listener, but the handler does nothing. Make each click update the cart count and status text. Keep the button usable by keyboard.

objectives.description: Update count and status when the button is clicked.
Explain the relationship between events, handlers, and state.

hints: The button already has addEventListener. Implement the function it calls.
Inside addItem, increase count, then update both text elements.
Set countLabel.textContent to the new count. Build the status message from the count.
count = count + 1; countLabel.textContent = String(count); status.textContent = count + (count === 1 ? " item in cart" : " items in cart");

misconceptions.description: Updating the label without changing stored count.
misconceptions.feedback: The visible label must reflect the stored count. If the count never changes, every click shows the same value.

misconceptions.description: Believing registering a listener performs the action.
misconceptions.feedback: Registering a listener tells the browser what to call later. The handler performs the action when the event occurs.

sections.title: Events connect input to code
sections.body: The browser emits an event when a user clicks, types, or presses a key. A listener registers a handler function for that event. The handler reads state, updates it, and changes the page.

sections.title: State must stay consistent
sections.body: The count variable and the visible text are two representations of the same fact. Updating one without the other produces a lie on screen. In larger applications, keeping state and rendering in step is a central design concern.

vocabulary.definition: A signal that something happened in the browser.
A registration that associates an event with a handler.
The function that runs when an event fires.

steps.title: Make the button respond
steps.prompt: Edit script.js so each click adds one item. The count and status must update, including singular and plural wording. Run the browser tests.

steps.title: What happens on click?
steps.prompt: Select every accurate statement about the cart.

statements.label: The click event calls the registered handler.

steps.explanation: A listener waits for an event. When it fires, the handler changes state and updates the page.
